title: The Global VM Lock
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of the global vm lock in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply the global vm lock in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to knowing when implementation details matter and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn The Global VM Lock through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding the global vm lock helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: The Global VM Lock helps you reason about mri implementation considerations. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: MRI implementation considerations. Then connect it to Impact on CPU-bound Ruby threads. The remaining syllabus points—I/O concurrency versus CPU parallelism, Knowing when implementation details matter—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Example: The Global VM Lock
content_blocks.code:
queue = Queue.new
worker = Thread.new { queue << "finished" }
puts queue.pop
worker.join

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports the global vm lock. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.text: Create a second example for the global vm lock using a different input. Add one edge case from the syllabus list (Knowing when implementation details matter), state the expected behavior, and write a small test or manual check that would catch a regression.

content_blocks.title: Recap

Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
